messages:
jen: kicking off batch-2 deploy now. plan: pin web-auth service to v2.3.4, enable feature flag `session-auth-v2` at 1% for canary, monitor logs/metrics for 15m, then slow shift to 10% -> 50% -> 100% if green. change window 02:00-04:00 UTC. release notes: https://confluence.redwood/products/release/2026-03-20-batch2 :eyes:
deploy-bot: deploy started by jen. created canary group `batch2-canary-1798024680`. applied pin web-auth@v2.3.4. feature flag action queued:
```
rbctl ff set session-auth-v2 --env prod --pct 1 --by batch2-canary-1798024680
```
deploy-bot: canary traffic now at 1% across prod regions. monitoring hooks attached (latency, 5xx rate, kv-cache hit rate).
mike: quick check — auth-proxy depends on the new header flow, can you confirm proxy pinned to 1.8.0?
jen: yep pinned auth-proxy@1.8.0 in the deploy manifest. leaving it pinned until 24h after full shift.
anya: staging ran unit/integration but e2e had flaky auth timeout on firefox. recommend hold at 1% until we see no increase in timeouts for 30m. :warning:
kevin: we should add a targeted health query against /healthz?include=auth to the canary probe. simple curl every 15s for the canary group. I'll attach the probe now.
kevin: probe snippet:
```
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" 'https://auth.redwood.internal/healthz?include=auth'
```
sre-oncall: rollback criteria proposal: if 5xx rate > 0.5% OR p50 latency +20% above baseline OR auth-specific timeouts increase by >30% over baseline within 15m, rollback to web-auth@v2.3.3 and ff session-auth-v2 -> 0%. also notify #incidents and page oncall if rollback triggers.
jen: agreed. will also capture sample traces for any 5xx. tagging traces with `deploy:batch2` so we can filter.
deploy-bot: canary 1%: 5m status update — p50 +12ms (within threshold), 5xx = 0.02%, auth timeout spikes not observed. logs: no new error signatures.
anya: LGTM to move to 10% after 15 additional minutes if metric stability holds.
jenn: (typo correction) jen: moving to 10% now. command:
```
rbctl ff set session-auth-v2 --env prod --pct 10 --by batch2-canary-1798024680
```
deploy-bot: session-auth-v2 set to 10%. rolling window 2m for propagation.
mike: re-checking downstream queued jobs; no sign of backlog. will keep an eye.
kevin: probe results for auth probe (last 3 samples): 200 0.024s, 200 0.022s, 200 0.025s. good.
sre-oncall: note — I've prepped a quick rollback command in vault: `rbctl deploy rollback web-auth --to v2.3.3 --reason "batch2 canary"` and an override to set ff to 0% in one step.
jen: if 10% stable for 30m we'll shift to 50%. keep pins until 24h post-100%. also adding a one-line release note summary to product channel after shift to 50%. :party:
deploy-bot: 10% status @ +18m — p50 steady, 5xx 0.03%, cache hit rate unchanged. no abnormal traces.
anya: approving move to 50% now. leaving e2e smoke running for another 10m.
jen: shifting to 50%:
```
rbctl ff set session-auth-v2 --env prod --pct 50 --by batch2-canary-1798024680
```
deploy-bot: session-auth-v2 set to 50%. watch window 15m.
mike: thumbs. monitoring job queue, auth-proxy still healthy.
sre-oncall: reminder: if we see auth timeout regression >30% revert immediately. paging config is ready.
deploy-bot: 50% status @ +12m — p50 +10ms, 5xx 0.04%, sample traces show a few 502s from a single instance in us-west-2. marking instance id i-0a12 and starting drain.
kevin: draining i-0a12 now; looks like a transient kernel upgrade job overlapped with the canary — unrelated to code.
jen: good catch. after drain metrics returned to baseline. proceed to full rollout.
jenn: (typo again) jen: moving to 100% and unpin version after 24h window:
```
rbctl ff set session-auth-v2 --env prod --pct 100 --by batch2-canary-1798024680
```
deploy-bot: session-auth-v2 100% applied. feature fully enabled. reminder: web-auth pinned to v2.3.4 until 2026-03-21T02:00:00Z.
anya: will run a final e2e sweep and post results.
sre-oncall: closing SRE watch in 30m if no regressions. rollback playbook archived under confluence page: https://confluence.redwood/ops/rollback-playbooks
jen: posting short release note to #product now and updating the release page. thanks everyone. :tada:
